title: Coefficient-limit embedding for cofinal monoid filtrations
statement:
Let $r\geq0$ be an integer, let $Q\subseteq\mathbf N^r$ be an additive submonoid, and let $L$ be a commutative ring with ideal $\mathfrak a$. Write $B=L[Q]$ for the ring of finite sums $\sum_{q\in Q}c_qz^q$, with $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$, and let $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put $|e|=\sum_i e_i$, $J=\mathfrak aB+(z^q:q\in Q\setminus\{0\})$, $I=\mathfrak aA+(X_1,\ldots,X_r)A$, and define $j:B\to A$ by $j(\sum_qc_qz^q)=\sum_qc_qX^q$. Assume that $L\to\varprojlim_k L/\mathfrak a^k$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], that $j(J)\subseteq I$, and that for every $n\geq0$ there is $N\geq n$ with $j^{-1}(I^N)\subseteq J^n$. Put $T=\varprojlim_n B/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], let $\eta:B\to T$ be the canonical map, and give $T$ the topology with basic neighborhoods $P_n=\ker(T\to B/J^n)$ and $A$ the topology with basic neighborhoods $I^n$. There is a unique continuous $L$-algebra homomorphism $\iota:T\to A$ satisfying $\iota\eta=j$. It is injective. For every $x=(x_n)_n\in T$, every choice of representatives $f_n\in B$ of $x_n$, and every $e\in\mathbf N^r$, the coefficient $c_e(\iota x)\in L$ is characterized by
$$c_e(\iota x)\equiv c_e(jf_n)\pmod{\mathfrak a^k}\quad(k\geq1,\ n\geq k+|e|).$$
This characterization is independent of all representatives. For every $n\geq0$ one has $\iota x-jf_n\in I^n$ and $\iota(P_n)\subseteq I^n$. Also $c_e(\iota x)=0$ for $e\notin Q$, the sequence $\eta(f_n)$ converges to $x$, and $\bigcap_n I^n=0$.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] to read the assumed injective completion map on $L$: an element in every $\mathfrak a^k$ has every residue zero and hence is zero. Thus $\bigcap_k\mathfrak a^k=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with coefficient ring $L$, base ideal $\mathfrak a$, and $d=r$. It gives $F\in I^n$ exactly when $c_e(F)\in\mathfrak a^{n-|e|}$ for all $|e|<n$. In particular $F\in\bigcap_n I^n$ implies $c_e(F)\in\mathfrak a^k$ by taking $n=k+|e|$, for every $k\geq1$. Every coefficient is zero, so $F=0$ by the family definition [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. This proves the asserted separation of $A$.

proof.text: The monomial formula for $j$ preserves sums, constants, and products: in the product, the coefficient at $e$ is the finite sum over $q+q'=e$, in both rings, by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Since $j(J)\subseteq I$, applying $j$ to finite sums of products gives $j(J^n)\subseteq I^n$. Fix $x=(x_n)\in T$ and representatives $f_n$. Compatibility in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] gives $f_m-f_n\in J^n$ whenever $m\geq n$. Consequently, for every $e$ and $k\geq1$, the residues $c_e(jf_n)\bmod\mathfrak a^k$ are independent of $n\geq k+|e|$: compare two indices at their minimum and use step 1. Changing a representative at such an index has the same effect, since its difference lies in $J^n$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: For fixed $e$, set $b_{e,k}=c_e(jf_{k+|e|})\bmod\mathfrak a^k$ for $k\geq1$ and use the unique residue at $k=0$. These residues are compatible: if $l\geq k\geq1$, step 2 compares indices $l+|e|$ and $k+|e|$ modulo $\mathfrak a^k$. The assumed bijection $L\to\varprojlim_k L/\mathfrak a^k$ in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] therefore supplies exactly one $c_e(x)\in L$ with these residues. Define $\iota(x)=\sum_e c_e(x)X^e$, an actual coefficient family as in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Step 2 gives the stated congruence for every allowed index and every choice of representatives. If two coefficient values satisfy all the congruences, their difference belongs to every $\mathfrak a^k$, so step 1 makes them equal. This proves both the characterization and its independence. For $e\notin Q$, all $c_e(jf_n)$ vanish; hence $c_e(x)=0$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: Operations in $T$ are componentwise by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $x,y\in T$ represented by $f_n,g_n$, representatives for $x+y$ and $xy$ are $f_n+g_n$ and $f_ng_n$. Fix $e,k$ and take $n\geq k+|e|$. The congruences of step 3 give $c_e(\iota(x+y))\equiv c_e(\iota x)+c_e(\iota y)\pmod{\mathfrak a^k}$. In the finite convolution for coefficient $e$, each pair $u+v=e$ has $|u|,|v|\leq|e|$, so the same index gives $c_e(\iota(xy))\equiv\sum_{u+v=e}c_u(\iota x)c_v(\iota y)\pmod{\mathfrak a^k}$. That sum is the product coefficient by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Separation in step 1 turns these congruences for all $k$ into equalities. For $x=\eta(b)$ choose $f_n=b$ for every $n$; step 3 then gives $\iota\eta(b)=j(b)$. In particular zero, one, and every scalar are preserved. Thus $\iota$ is an $L$-algebra homomorphism extending $j$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and $|e|<n$, and put $k=n-|e|\geq1$. The coefficient congruence from step 3 applies at the index $n=k+|e|$ itself, giving $c_e(\iota x-jf_n)\in\mathfrak a^{n-|e|}$. The criterion [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients], for arbitrary $L$ and $\mathfrak a$, yields $\iota x-jf_n\in I^n$. For $n=0$ this is automatic because $I^0=A$. If $x\in P_n$, its representative $f_n$ lies in $J^n$ since $x_n=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; step 2 puts $jf_n\in I^n$, and the just-proved difference gives $\iota x\in I^n$. Thus $\iota(P_n)\subseteq I^n$ for every $n$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: If $\iota x=0$, fix $n$ and choose the assumed $N\geq n$ with $j^{-1}(I^N)\subseteq J^n$. Step 5 at index $N$ gives $jf_N\in I^N$, whence $f_N\in J^n$. Compatibility of the coordinates of $x$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] says that the image of $f_N$ in $B/J^n$ is $x_n$, so $x_n=0$. This holds for every $n$ and therefore $x=0$. Since $\iota$ is additive, equality of two images reduces to this zero-kernel assertion by subtraction; hence $\iota$ is injective.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: The inclusions $\iota(P_n)\subseteq I^n$ prove continuity directly: if $y-x\in P_n$, additivity gives $\iota(y)-\iota(x)\in I^n$, for the basic neighborhoods specified in the statement. For every $m$ and $n\geq m$, compatibility in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] says that $\eta(f_n)-x$ has zero $m$-th coordinate, so it belongs to $P_m$. This is exactly convergence $\eta(f_n)\to x$ for that neighborhood basis. No assertion $P_m=J^mT$, finite generation, or completeness of $T$ for extended ideal powers is being used.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 (PDF p. 76), motivates the completed monoid models only; the following coefficient argument is agent-written, using the existing coefficient criterion and the inverse-limit definition (Stacks Tags 00M9, section-completion, and 0317, definition-complete).

proof.text: Let $g:T\to A$ be any continuous $L$-algebra homomorphism with $g\eta=j$. Fix $x$ and $h\geq1$. Continuity at $x$ gives $m$ such that $y-x\in P_m$ implies $g(y)-g(x)\in I^h$. Choose $n\geq m,h$. Step 7 gives $\eta(f_n)-x\in P_m$, hence $jf_n-g(x)\in I^h$. Step 5 gives $\iota x-jf_n\in I^n\subseteq I^h$. Adding shows $\iota x-g(x)\in I^h$. This holds for all $h$, so step 1 forces $g(x)=\iota x$. It proves uniqueness for every $x$ and finishes all the claims.
